newsitem.title: CANADA: New Zealand joins accord for smoke-free flights.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand joins accord for smoke-free flights.

text.p: New Zealand Monday announced it joined a treaty already signed by the United States, Canada and Australia that bans smoking on many international flights.
New Zealand Transport Minister Jenny Shipley announced the move during a meeting in Canada of transport ministers from Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum countries.
The accord bans smoking on non-stop flights between the four countries that have signed it.
New Zealand intended to sign the agreement with the other countries in 1994 but had to implement changes to its laws first.

While New Zealand's participation officially begins in two months, Air New Zealand has voluntarily reduced the number of its flights that allow smoking since 1992. The New Zealand government last year banned smoking on all international flights operated by New Zealand carriers except those to Japan and South Korea.
Shipley said a ban to those two countries was also under consideration. Ministers from the four countries participating in the agreement said they hoped other countries would follow suit.
